summary.text: Erik Martin Dilan was first sworn into the Assembly in 2015 and represents the 54th District, covering parts of Bedford-Stuyvesant, Bushwick, Cypress Hills and East New York in Brooklyn.
His official biography says he chairs the Correction Committee and previously served 12 years on the New York City Council.

paragraphs.text: Dilan was born in Bushwick on May 11, 1974, to former state Senator Martin Malave-Dilan and Debra Dilan, and attended New York City public schools, according to his Assembly biography.
He received an associate degree in business administration from St. John's University.
He began his public service on Community School Board 32 and also served on Brooklyn Community Board 4.
Before the Assembly, Dilan served 12 years on the City Council, where he chaired the Housing and Buildings Committee and the Brooklyn Delegation and was on the budget negotiating team.
In 2023 he was appointed chair of the Assembly Correction Committee, and he also sits on the Energy, Insurance and Ways and Means Committees.

The biography lists legislation he passed on disability protections for support animals, identification for people released from prison, and emergency-contact notification when an incarcerated person is hospitalized.
He lives in Cypress Hills with his wife, Jannitza, and their children.
